 Stray Kids to Play 46 Concerts in 31 Cities as Run It Tour Expands From Seoul to Milan
 JYP Entertainment confirms 25 new Run It concert dates in North America, Europe and Japan, bringing Stray Kids' fourth world tour to 46 shows across 31 cities through July 31, 2027.
 Clara Espinoza 
/
 Published Nov 10 2026, 9:40 AM EST Share on Twitter 
 Share on Facebook 
 Share on WhatsApp 
 Members of the South Korean K-pop group Stray Kids perform during the last week of the Rock in Rio music festival at the Rio 2016 Olympic Park in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, on September 12, 2026. 
 Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images 
 The Briefing: 
 JYP Entertainment announced Monday that Stray Kids will add 25 shows in 23 cities across Japan, North America, and Europe to the Run It World Tour, raising the total to 46 concerts in 31 cities through July 31, 2027.
 The North American leg spans 14 dates from May 16 to June 29, 2027, with confirmed stops in Seattle, Los Angeles, Chicago, Toronto, and East Rutherford, New Jersey, among others; a seven-show European stretch closes in Milan.
 Run It launched July 25, 2026 in Seoul with five consecutive sold-out nights and has since moved through Japan, Hong Kong, Taipei, Bangkok, and Singapore, supporting the group's tenth Korean EP This & That .
 Stray Kids are going west. JYP Entertainment announced Monday that the group will add 25 concerts in 23 cities to the ongoing Run It World Tour, formally extending the fourth world tour of their career into North America and Europe — with a final curtain call set for Milan, Italy, on July 31, 2027.

 Before any Western date was on the books, the Run It tour had already delivered some of the most in-demand K-pop concerts of the year. The tour opened in Seoul on July 25, 2026, with five consecutive nights at KSPO Dome selling out across the board. Stray Kids then swept through Japan with dome and stadium dates in Tokyo — including three nights at Tokyo Dome in November — plus stops in Nagoya, Osaka, and Fukuoka, before heading to Kai Tak Stadium in Hong Kong on December 5, Taipei Dome on December 12, and two-night stands in Bangkok (January 16–17, 2027) and Singapore (March 6–7, 2027). 
 North America: 14 Dates, Coast to Coast 
 The North American leg opens May 16, 2027, and runs through June 29. Fourteen shows stretch from the Pacific Northwest to the Eastern Seaboard, with confirmed stops in Seattle, Vancouver, Santa Clara, San Diego, Los Angeles, Arlington, Houston, Atlanta, Miami, Orlando, Chicago, Baltimore, Toronto, and East Rutherford, New Jersey — a short distance from New York City. Before crossing the Pacific, Stray Kids will return to Japan for additional shows in Yokohama on April 24 and 25, and Osaka on May 4 and 5. 
 Europe: Paris to Milan 
 Seven European concerts follow the North American run, kicking off July 9, 2027. The group will play Paris, London, Munich, Vienna, Barcelona, and Arnhem in the Netherlands before bringing the entire campaign to a close in Milan on July 31 — the final night of a world tour that will have stretched across more than 13 months. All 46 dates combined place Stray Kids before audiences in 31 cities across three continents. 
 The Music Powering the Tour 
 Run It was engineered as a full creative campaign from the outset. The pre-release single "Run It" dropped June 24, 2026, and topped iTunes charts across multiple markets before the full album had even a confirmed release date. On August 7, Stray Kids released This & That , their tenth Korean-language EP — eight tracks produced entirely by in-house unit 3RACHA, featuring members Bang Chan, Changbin, and Han. The tour also backs Suiatsu , the group's fifth Japanese-language EP, anchoring their status as one of the most consistently sold-out live acts in that market. 
 Two fans pose in front of posters of K-pop boy band Stray Kids before attending the band's concert, which kicked off a world tour, in Seoul on July 25, 2026. 
 Photo by GREG BAKER / AFP via Getty Images 
 Standing on the Shoulders of dominATE 
 The scope of Run It becomes sharper when measured against what preceded it. The dominATE World Tour wrapped in October 2025 after 56 shows across 35 cities, standing at the time as the most ambitious concert run in Stray Kids' history. Run It, with 46 confirmed dates, doesn't surpass dominATE in total show count — but it trades density for geographic reach, planting the group in European capitals and North American markets that generated enormous unmet demand during the dominATE cycle. The decision to scale into some of the continent's largest venues signals a level of ambition few K-pop acts have pursued this aggressively. 
 Presale and on-sale dates for the North American and European legs have not yet been announced. Given the speed with which Asian dates sold out, competition for tickets when they go live is expected to be intense.
